hypotheses.mechanism: Executing Q4_FAST decode during warmup changes GPU/cache/clock/driver state and causally slows the immediately following identical prefill.
hypotheses.discriminating_prediction: With both safe and fast decode chains prepared in the same process/resource footprint, switching only the warmup decode chain changes subsequent identical-prefill TTFT/GPU-prefill time.
hypotheses.falsifier: No stable post-warmup TTFT/GPU-prefill difference under shared resource footprint.

hypotheses.mechanism: Preparing the fast decode chain changes driver/pipeline/descriptor resource state enough to slow subsequent identical prefill even when no decode warmup is executed.
hypotheses.discriminating_prediction: Safe-only vs fast-only prepared decode-chain processes differ in prefill latency under identical no-decode conditioning.
hypotheses.falsifier: No stable difference under no-decode conditioning.

hypotheses.mechanism: The regression is primarily CPU/driver command recording, queue submission, or fence-wait overhead rather than GPU prefill execution.
hypotheses.discriminating_prediction: CPU-side TTFT component increases while GPU timestamped prefill duration does not increase proportionally.
hypotheses.falsifier: Regression is localized to GPU timestamped prefill execution.

hypotheses.mechanism: The identical prefill command stream runs slower on GPU because prior decode execution leaves an unfavorable cache/clock/thermal/residency state.
hypotheses.discriminating_prediction: GPU timestamped prefill duration increases after fast-decode conditioning under shared resource footprint.
hypotheses.falsifier: GPU timestamped duration unchanged while host-side components account for regression.

hypotheses.mechanism: The P6 TTFT gap is primarily process/order/clock-ramping bias rather than a stable architecture-dependent carryover mechanism.
hypotheses.discriminating_prediction: Counterbalanced fresh processes with neutral conditioning erase or reverse the candidate/reference gap; within-process shared-footprint conditioning shows no fast-vs-safe causal effect.
hypotheses.falsifier: Within-process randomized shared-footprint fast-vs-safe conditioning reproduces the effect.
